articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 vulnerabilities like it's hot, including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Chrome patches its fourth zero-day this year because apparently browsers are made of Swiss cheese.

articles.title: Meta U-turns on encryption push for Instagram as DMs go plaintext
articles.summary: 'Dirty Frag' Linux flaw gives root access with a public exploit and zero patches—because nothing says responsible disclosure like dropping a root exploit with no CVE. Admins everywhere just felt their souls leave their bodies.

articles.title: cPanel, WHM Release Fixes for Three New Vulnerabilities — Patch Now
articles.summary: Ollama's out-of-bounds read vulnerability lets attackers slurp entire process memory from 300,000+ servers remotely. It's like leaving your diary open, but the diary contains everyone's secrets.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: ShinyHunters crashes Canvas during finals week, holding student data hostage while kids nationwide panic about their grades. Nothing says 'chaos' like attacking education during crunch time.

articles.title: Congress Narrowed the GUARD Act, But Serious Problems Remain
articles.summary: Russian military hackers pwned ancient routers to harvest Microsoft Office tokens en masse. When your security strategy relies on routers older than TikTok, you're gonna have a bad time.

articles.title: Hackers ate my homework: Educational SaaS Canvas down after cyberattack
articles.summary: Meta abandons Instagram DM encryption after years of promising privacy, giving Zuckerberg full visibility into your thirst traps again. Privacy theater reaches its final act with a standing ovation from surveillance capitalism.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as a criminal offense worthy of arrest and strip searches. The same administration that perfected the art of records evasion suddenly discovers transparency religion.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft for SMS phishing campaigns. Another brilliant mind learns that cybercrime pays poorly when you get caught.

articles.title: U.S. Fuel Exports Hit Record High as Hormuz Crisis Reshapes Global Energy Flows
articles.summary: Anthropic's Mythos AI discovers thousands of zero-days across major OS and browsers, prompting Fed chair to frantically call bank CEOs. When AI starts finding vulns faster than humans can patch them, we're officially in the endgame.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Mythos found thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities. The Fed chair called the banks.
articles.summary: Intruder builds AI that does $50K manual pentests in minutes, making expensive security consultants sweat harder than their overpriced reports. The robots aren't just coming for blue-collar jobs anymore.
